Our TPP focuses on improvement in bone pain and physical functioning, but we also need to capture fatigue and treatment tolerability. Please generate a full COA strategy.

## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

**In one sentence:** Demonstrate patient-perceived benefit from a novel proteasome inhibitor in symptomatic improvement (bone pain, physical functioning, fatigue) while maintaining treatment tolerability in heavily pretreated RRMM patients.

**Key challenge:** Achieving confirmatory PRO endpoints within hierarchical testing when 98% of KG MM trials positioned PRO as secondary only, requiring upstream clinical endpoints to achieve significance first.

**Recommended starting point:** EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 + EQ-5D-5L based on consistent use across comparator trials [TI-001, TI-004, TI-005] and regulatory acceptance for MM submissions [IR-003, IR-004, IR-005].

**Critical gap:** Domain Coverage Matrix not available in KG — expert must verify coverage of FDA core domains including disease-related bone pain and proteasome inhibitor-specific neuropathy monitoring.

## Key Observations

• **PRO endpoint positioning uniformity**: 98% of KG MM trials (52/53 records) used PRO as secondary endpoints, with hierarchical testing dependency on upstream clinical endpoints — positioning strategy should align with this precedent unless compelling scientific rationale exists for deviation. Expert must consider whether PFS/OS endpoints are sufficiently powered to enable PRO testing.

• **EORTC instrument performance variability**: QLQ-C30 achieved significant changes in AQUILA and CARTITUDE-4 [TI-001, TI-005] but failed to detect changes in DREAMM-7/8 [TI-002, TI-003], suggesting sensitivity may depend on mechanism of action or patient population characteristics. ADC mechanisms (belantamab mafodotin) showed null PRO results across multiple domains.

• **PRO-CTCAE emergence in recent trials**: Both DREAMM-7 and CARTITUDE-4 included PRO-CTCAE for symptomatic adverse event capture [TI-002, TI-005], indicating regulatory expectation for patient-reported tolerability assessment in MM submissions. Critical for proteasome inhibitor-associated neuropathy monitoring.

• **Novel instrument adoption**: CARTITUDE-4 successfully used MySIm-Q (14-20 items) as MM-specific instrument with significant results (p<0.001) [TI-005], though regulatory acceptance not established [IR-007] — represents potential innovation but regulatory risk. MCID data expected March 2026 from MajesTEC-3 population.

• **EQ-5D-5L consistency for HTA**: Successfully detected changes in daratumumab-based regimens (AQUILA) and CAR-T (CARTITUDE-4) but not collected in DREAMM trials [TI-001, TI-005] — mandatory for NICE QALY calculations and strongly preferred by ICER for US value assessments. Without EQ-5D, UK reimbursement severely compromised.

• **Missing data and multiplicity control as rejection drivers**: FDA rejection patterns show systematic issues with hierarchical testing failure [REJ-019], no multiplicity adjustment [REJ-031, REJ-032], and excessive missing data [REJ-039] — prespecification and alpha control architecture must be established before instrument selection.

## Comparator Analysis

**Same-mechanism proteasome inhibitor evidence:**
- **carfilzomib** [COMP-001]: Used EORTC QLQ-C30 GHS/QoL scale only, EMA-accepted — suggests regulatory precedent for focused QLQ-C30 subscales rather than full instrument battery
- **ixazomib** [COMP-002]: Combined EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20, EMA-accepted — established precedent for this instrument pairing in PI trials  
- **bortezomib** [COMP-003]: No PRO data reported — represents unmet need for patient experience characterization in PI class

**Cross-mechanism insights:**
- **melphalan flufenamide** [COMP-004]: EMA-rejected with no PRO instruments recorded — reinforces importance of robust PRO strategy for regulatory differentiation
- **panobinostat** [COMP-005]: EMA-rejected, no PRO instruments — HDAC + PI combination showed null PRO results [REJ-038]

**Based on comparator evidence, EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 combination has the strongest regulatory signal in proteasome inhibitor trials, with both carfilzomib and ixazomib achieving EMA acceptance using this approach [COMP-001, COMP-002].**

## HTA Requirements

| HTA Body | Required Instrument | In candidate list? | Action needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| NICE | EQ-5D-5L | Yes (TBD) | Include with England value set (Devlin 2018) |
| ICER | EQ-5D-5L (preferred) | Yes (TBD) | Include for QALY calculation |

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Instrument selection from missing Domain Coverage Matrix** — verify coverage of FDA core domains and select minimal viable battery balancing patient burden with regulatory coverage.

2. **Hierarchical testing positioning** — determine whether PRO endpoints can realistically achieve confirmatory status given upstream PFS/OS power assumptions and historical 0% primary PRO rate in MM trials.

3. **Proteasome inhibitor-specific neuropathy monitoring** — decide whether PRO-CTCAE, CIPN-20, or alternative neuropathy-specific instruments are required given mechanism-specific toxicity profile.

4. **Assessment schedule optimization** — align PRO timepoints with step-up dosing schedule in Cycle 1 and weekly administration pattern to capture tolerability during dose escalation phase.

5. **Alpha allocation strategy** — establish multiplicity control hierarchy that positions PRO endpoints to achieve significance, learning from rejection patterns showing hierarchical testing failure as leading cause of MM PRO claim rejection [REJ-019, REJ-031].
